name: The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion

relationships.label: The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion is the official state religion of the Pale Dominion — all Dominion law, policy, and culture derives from its teachings.
The Doctrine venerates Yssara of the Shattered Moon as the divine source of all lunar magic — the moon fragment at the Pale Spire is her living presence on earth.
The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion is founded on the Arch-Seers' interpretation of the First Moon Ritual — they codified what the First Voice discovered into sacred law.
The Pale Spire is the holy city of the Doctrine — the moon fragment at its center is the seat of Yssara's power and the residence of the Arch-Seers.
The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion considers the Cult of the Broken Moon's interpretation of Yssara heretical — the Cult views the moon fragment as liberation, not instruction.

description: The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion is the official state religion of the Pale Dominion, a cold, clinical faith that teaches that the corruption spreading through Northern Velkaris is not a curse but a sacred process. The hierarchy of the Dominion is a hierarchy of the damaged — those who have sacrificed the most fragments of their soul stand closest to Yssara. The Doctrine strips the terror from self-destruction and rebrands it as liturgy. There is no sin, only miscalculation. No damnation, only incomplete dissolution. No prayer, only protocol.
excerpt: The official state religion of the Pale Dominion — a cold, clinical faith that rebrands self-destruction as liturgy and measures holiness by how much of the soul has been sacrificed.
content:
The world is breaking. This is not a tragedy. It is the natural state of all things, and to resist it is to deny the truth that Yssara revealed when she shattered the moon. The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion teaches that corruption is not a flaw — it is a process, and the only sin is to let it happen without purpose. The body decays. The mind frays. The soul erodes with every spell cast. These are not losses. They are offerings.

The hierarchy of the Dominion is a hierarchy of the damaged. Those who have sacrificed the most fragments of their soul stand closest to Yssara. The Arch-Seers have given more of themselves than any living person — their memories are scarred, their emotions flattened, their sense of self reduced to a single, certain purpose. They are not broken. They are refined. The lower ranks are measured by what they are willing to lose. A novice who offers a finger is respected. A priest who offers a decade of memory is revered. An Arch-Seer who has offered everything is beyond judgment.

The clinical language of the Doctrine is deliberate. There is no sin, only miscalculation. No damnation, only incomplete dissolution. No prayer, only protocol. The First Moon Ritual is not a sacred mystery — it is a documented procedure, recorded in the Scriptoriums of the Pale Spire with the precision of an anatomical diagram. The moon fragment at the Spire's center does not radiate holiness. It radiates a measurable field. The Doctrine's greatest innovation was to strip the terror from self-destruction and rebrand it as liturgy.

attributes.tenets: Corruption is sacred; self-destruction is worship; the damaged are the holy; the soul is fuel; doubt is the only sin
attributes.clergy: The Arch-Seers of the Pale Dominion — a hierarchy measured by soul-fragments sacrificed
attributes.holy_text: The Canon of the Fragment — a codified collection of ritual procedures and theological interpretations
attributes.rituals: The Daily Offering (soul-fragment sacrifice); the Rite of Codification (study of the First Moon Ritual); the Purge of Heretics
attributes.schism: The Cult of the Broken Moon split from the Doctrine over the interpretation of the First Moon Ritual — liberation versus instruction

name: The Hollow Covenant

relationships.label: The Hollow Covenant venerates Mourne the Hollow King as the central deity of their faith — he is not feared but revered, for he collects the souls of the forgotten and gives them purpose.
The Hollow Covenant is the folk religion of the Oathbound Remnants and Greyvast survivors — it has no clergy, no hierarchy, only shared grief and sworn oaths.
The Hollow Covenant was born in the mist-choked ruins of Greyvast, forged by survivors who had lost everything and found meaning in the act of remembering.
The Hollow Covenant stands in direct theological opposition to the Doctrine of Controlled Erosion — grief versus purification, memory versus purpose, folk versus institution.

description: The Hollow Covenant is the folk religion of the Oathbound Remnants — a grief-soaked, oral tradition with no clergy, no hierarchy, only shared loss and sworn oaths. Its central belief is that Mourne the Hollow King hunts the forgotten, and that to be remembered is to be saved. The Covenant has no temples because the dead do not need roofs. It has no priests because grief requires no intermediary. It has no scripture because the names on Mournwall's wall are the only text that matters.
excerpt: The folk religion of the Oathbound Remnants — raw, grief-soaked, no clergy, no hierarchy. Carve names into stone so Mourne won't forget you.
content:
Mourne does not answer prayers. He collects.

That is the first truth of the Hollow Covenant, and the only one that matters. The Covenant has no temples because the dead do not need roofs. It has no priests because grief requires no intermediary. It has no scripture because the names on Mournwall's wall are the only text that matters. Every night, the Remnants read the names aloud. Every name that is spoken is a soul that Mourne has not yet taken.

The oaths are the Covenant's only ritual. They are sworn on the Name Wall, hand to stone, voice to mist. There is no written record of the oath because the oath is not a contract — it is a declaration made to Mourne directly. Break it, and the Hollow King will know. He will find your name in the dark, and he will cross it out. The Remnants do not fear death. They fear erasure. They carve names into stone, sing names into the mist, whisper names to their children, because every name spoken is a name Mourne cannot take.

attributes.tenets: To be remembered is to be saved; to forget is the only true death; oaths are sworn to Mourne directly; grief is the highest form of worship
attributes.clergy: None — the Covenant has no priests, no hierarchy, no institution
attributes.holy_text: The Name Wall at Mournwall — the only scripture is the carved names of the dead
attributes.rituals: The Nightly Roll Call (reading of the dead); the Oath-Swearing (hand to the Name Wall); the Rite of Memory (oral history transmission)
attributes.schism: None — the Covenant has no orthodoxy to fracture
